_doc: PHASE_2_NAVIGATION_AND_GATHERING.md §3.2 — kind -> anchor rule, resolved
at query time by TargetRegistry.queryNearby (iteration 2.8) and turned
into a real walkable point by anchor resolution (iteration 2.9).
'radial': sample `slots`-independent points on a circle of `radius`
around the target, discard non-walkable, pick nearest to the agent.
'fixed': a single point at `offset` in the target's own local frame,
rotated by rot*90 degrees, facing `facing` quarter-turns.
fishing's fallbackRadius is NOT authored here as a literal — it is
POND.radius + 4, computed in config/index.ts's anchorRuleFor() from the
real pond definition (game/data/world.ts), so it can never drift out of
sync with the pond's actual size the way a second hardcoded number could.
AUTHORING RULE for a 'radial' rule, learned the hard way from the barrel
(Wave 10 verification): a target's OWN footprint is stamped into the nav
grid inflated by AGENT_RADIUS (0.55m, game/navgrid.ts) and then rounded
OUT to whole cells (cellSize 1.0 everywhere, ai/config/navgrid.json), so
the blocked square around a piece reaches up to `halfSize + 0.55 + 1`
from its centre. A `radius` smaller than that can never produce a
walkable sample — every one of the 8 lands inside the piece's own
blocked footprint — and resolution falls entirely to nearestWalkable,
whose budget is `ceil(fallbackRadius / cellSize)` CELLS. The barrel had
radius 0.9 with no fallbackRadius, which is a 1-cell budget inside a
3-4 cell blocked square: resolveAnchor returned null for every barrel
ever placed, so haul_to_deposit read 'blocked' and a villager carrying a
load to one stood there holding it forever. Keep radius clear of the
inflated footprint AND leave the fallback at least 2-3 cells of room.
